tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company was entitled to excise duty incentives for the assessment years 2006-07 to 2015-16 for its Gagal plant located in the state of Himachal Pradesh. ACC has been contending that the said incentives are in the nature of capital receipts and hence not liable to income tax. However, the Income tax department had consistently denied the position and considered these incentives as a taxable receipt. Post receipt of favourable orders from ITAT, Mumbai, the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) in subsequent years have also passed the orders in favour of the company. Consequently, the Revenue Authorities have also passed necessary order giving effect to ITAT Orders and consequential refunds have also been granted. Accordingly. the management has assessed the risk to be remote and reduced the contingent liability for this matter to nil.

The company has received Assessment Order for the FY 2019-20 demanding Rs. 102.45 crores towards certain disallowances. The company had filed appeal against the said order which is pending for disposal.

guidance.statement: FY27 cement demand growth expected soft at ~5%
Total cement cost to fall by ₹150–200 per tonne in FY27 from ~₹4,400/t in FY26
Capacity utilisation to rise from 77% to 85%

industry: Commodities > Construction Materials > Cement & Cement Products

operating_notes.text: Ambuja consolidated cement capacity was 109 MTPA on 31 March 2026, rising to ~119 MTPA after H1FY27 projects.
ACC's Q4FY26 cement sales volume was 11.9 MnT at 80% capacity utilisation, up 8% YoY.
Imported petcoke CFR rose 35% in Q4FY26 to USD 160/t, driving fuel cost inflation.
Cost reduction of ₹206 PMT achieved sequentially through focused optimization initiatives
Trade share increased to 78% with premium cement at 34% of trade sales
Blended cement share improved to 85% with clinker factor at 63.7%
